masthead.deck: Video games, home computers, software counters, and culture for the week of November 22-28, 1982

layoutPlan.lead: Vectrex turns a built-in vector screen into a holiday counter spectacle
secondary: Atari 5200 and the renamed 2600 share the November aisle
Choplifter keeps the Apple II game chart lively

editorNote: The 1982 holiday counter is crowded: Atari movie cartridges and premium consoles share space with home-computer memory claims, while E.T. keeps the box-office crown and Lionel Richie tops the singles chart.
morningLine: Atari movie games and 64K home-computer pitches crowd the early-December holiday shelf.

lead.headline: Atari Movie Cartridges Crowd the Holiday Counter
lead.summary: Atari entered the Christmas aisle with high-profile licensed cartridges including E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Raiders of the Lost Ark for the 2600, turning familiar movie names into front-of-store game pitches as buyers compared consoles, cartridges, and new home computers.
lead.confidence: November 1982 release records for both Atari 2600 cartridges; holiday-week retail framing inferred from the December shopping calendar.

computerItems.label: Game Shelf
computerItems.headline: E.T. Arrives as a Fast-Turnaround Atari Bet
computerItems.summary: The Atari 2600 E.T. cartridge, released in November 1982, gives stores a direct tie to the year's biggest film even as buyers still have to learn its maze-like play from the manual.
computerItems.confidence: November 1982 release verified; gameplay and retail emphasis are period context.

computerItems.label: Adventure Counter
computerItems.headline: Raiders of the Lost Ark Joins the 2600 Map
computerItems.summary: Howard Scott Warshaw's Raiders of the Lost Ark cartridge brings an inventory-and-map adventure to the 2600, another sign that licensed film properties are becoming a major console strategy.

computerItems.label: Home Computer Desk
computerItems.headline: Commodore 64 Keeps Selling 64K as the Hook
computerItems.summary: Commodore's 1982 machine gives dealers a simple comparison line: 64K RAM, color graphics, sound, and a price that can be weighed against game consoles and lower-memory home computers.
computerItems.confidence: 1982 launch and period positioning; not exact-day specific.

computerItems.label: Vector Corner
computerItems.headline: Vectrex Demonstrations Still Stop Shoppers
computerItems.summary: General Consumer Electronics' self-contained Vectrex remains a distinctive holiday-floor display because its built-in vector monitor looks unlike television-based cartridge systems.
computerItems.confidence: November 1982 launch window; December retail presence inferred.

softwareList.name: VisiCalc
softwareList.detail: Still the spreadsheet name many buyers recognize when a computer is justified for home finance or small business.

softwareList.name: WordStar
softwareList.detail: A familiar word-processing package in office and serious home-computing conversations.

softwareList.name: AtariWriter
softwareList.detail: Atari's word processor gives the home-computer aisle a practical pitch beyond games.

softwareList.name: Microsoft BASIC
softwareList.detail: Built-in or bundled BASIC remains the language many shoppers expect to see demonstrated.

priceWatch.note: Aggressive 64K memory pitch for the home-computer aisle.
Premium console positioning for the holiday season.
Licensed movie games compete for gift budgets.

market.headline: Holiday Buyers Compare Consoles With Computers
market.summary: The early-December sales floor is less about one clear winner than about competing promises: arcade-style cartridges, famous movie licenses, 64K home computers, and practical software for families trying to justify the purchase.
market.confidence: Synthesis from verified 1982 product releases and holiday timing.

bbsNote.headline: Modem Note
bbsNote.summary: The mass market is still focused on consoles and low-cost computers, while 300-baud callers trade settings, game hints, and local phone numbers after hours.

curiosity.headline: Cinema Lobby
curiosity.summary: Box Office Mojo lists E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial as the No. 1 domestic film for the December 3-5, 1982 weekend, keeping the movie in front of families seeing E.T. cartridge pitches.

briefs.headline: E.T. Still Leads Theaters
briefs.summary: Box Office Mojo lists E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial at No. 1 for the December 3-5 domestic weekend, ahead of An Officer and a Gentleman and First Blood.

briefs.headline: Empire Re-Release Holds Fourth
briefs.summary: The 1982 re-release of The Empire Strikes Back remains in the top five for the same weekend, adding another familiar movie brand to the season.

briefs.headline: Maneater Climbs the Singles Race
briefs.summary: Music Charts Archive lists Daryl Hall and John Oates' Maneater at No. 4 on the December 4 Billboard Hot 100 chart.

periodAd.headline: Holiday Special: Bring The Arcade Home
periodAd.summary: Ask for Atari movie cartridges, ColecoVision arcade favorites, Vectrex vector action, and Commodore 64 demonstrations at your local computer counter.
periodAd.confidence: Composite period-style advertisement based on verified products.

classifieds.headline: BASIC tutoring
classifieds.copy: Evening lessons for new home-computer owners. Bring your manual and cassette recorder.

classifieds.headline: Cartridge swap
classifieds.copy: 2600 owners meet Saturday to trade duplicates before Christmas.

worldFallback.headline: Editors Hold the Front to Games
worldFallback.summary: No routine world or sports item displaces this week's console, software, and culture story.
